questions.q: What problem does a Terraform module solve, per this lesson?
options: Needing the same set of resources across multiple environments without copy-pasting the same resource blocks repeatedly
Making Terraform files run faster
Removing the need for a resource group
Replacing the need for providers
questions.explain: Lessons 8-10's resources are needed in dev, staging, and prod — a module avoids maintaining three separate copies of the same blocks.

questions.q: What is a Terraform module, structurally?
options: A folder of .tf files with its own variable and output declarations
A special binary plugin separate from regular Terraform files
A single resource block marked with a module keyword
A JSON configuration file unrelated to HCL
questions.explain: A module is just parameterized Terraform files in their own folder — nothing more exotic than that.

questions.q: What does the source argument in a module block point to?
options: The module's folder (or registry path) containing its .tf files
The Azure subscription ID
The name of the resource group being created
The Terraform state file
questions.explain: source tells Terraform where to find the module's own configuration files.

questions.q: If you fix a bug inside modules/data-landing-zone/main.tf, what has to change in the module blocks that call it?
options: Nothing — the fix applies to every environment that calls the module the next time apply runs
Every module block must be rewritten to include the fix manually
The module must be renamed
Each environment's variables must be updated to match the fix
questions.explain: That's the entire point of a module — one definition, automatically applied everywhere it's called.

questions.q: What determines whether something inside a module is reachable from the code that calls it?
options: Whether it's declared as an output — anything not output stays internal to the module
Whether it's the first resource block in the file
Whether it has a tags block
Whether the module has a variable of the same name
questions.explain: Outputs are the only part of a module visible to its caller; everything else stays internal.
